mainEntity.name: How do local summer temperatures in Cottonwood and Cornville affect workshop conversion planning?

acceptedAnswer.text: In high-heat desert environments like Cottonwood and Cornville, managing summer heat gain is the top priority. Metal roofs and thin siding can cause interior temperatures to soar past 110 degrees without adequate thermal breaks and high R-value insulation. Closed-cell spray foam or continuous rigid foam works well because it creates an air barrier that blocks heat transfer and eliminates radiant condensation. Selecting an appropriately sized heat pump with strong cooling efficiency is critical to keeping the space comfortable during prolonged triple-digit summer afternoons.
acceptedAnswer.description: Intense summer heat requires robust insulation, radiant barriers, and properly sized heat pumps to keep the workshop comfortable through triple-digit temperatures.
